title: "AI Engineering at Scale"
subtitle: "Semester 2: Distributed Systems & Fleets — Week-by-Week"

## Course Overview

| | |
|:---|:---|
| **Textbook** | Volume II: Scaling Machine Learning Systems |
| **Duration** | 16 weeks (32 lectures at 75 min each) |
| **Prerequisites** | Foundations semester (Volume I) or equivalent systems background |
| **Scope** | Multi-machine distributed systems: clusters to global fleets |
| **Key Concepts** | 3D parallelism, collective communication, fault tolerance, fleet orchestration |

**Course Goal**: Defend distributed AI system designs and operating decisions using supplied workloads, measurements, and analytical models. Students will reason about coordinating thousands of accelerators, recovering valid progress after failures, and serving fleet demand under quality, cost, energy, and affected-population constraints.

::: {.callout-note}
## Labs and TinyTorch in Semester 2
Each week's table pairs the reading with its reinforcing lab. Complete the reading before the lab and submit the listed Decision Log by the end of that week. Week 15 includes two labs; Lab 17 contributes to the capstone submission in week 16. Volume II focuses on systems design rather than framework implementation, so there is no TinyTorch column. Modules 09–20 are available as an [optional advanced track](https://mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch/) for students continuing from Semester 1.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Lecture Slides
Each chapter has a companion Beamer slide deck with speaker notes, timing guidance, and active learning exercises. Available as PDF, PowerPoint, and LaTeX source at [mlsysbook.ai/slides](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/vol2.html).
:::

## Part I: The Fleet (Weeks 1–4) {#part-i}

*Goal: Build the physical computer the size of a campus.*

### Week 1: The Scale Imperative

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Introduction to Scale](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/introduction/introduction.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 01](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_01_introduction/): The Scale Wall |
| **Due** | Lab 01 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Explain why single-machine optimization hits a ceiling. Quantify the compute requirements of frontier model training. Articulate the transition from "fast machine" to "coordinated fleet."

::: {.callout-tip}
## Instructor Tip
Start with a question: "Public estimates put GPT-4 training at ~25,000 GPUs for about three months. What happens when one fails?" This sets up the problem the semester addresses.
:::

### Week 2: Compute Infrastructure

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Compute Infrastructure](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/compute_infrastructure/compute_infrastructure.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 02](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_02_compute_infra/): The Interconnect Wall |
| **Due** | Lab 02 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Describe the hierarchy from chip → node → rack → pod → cluster. Calculate bisection bandwidth for a given network topology. Explain why NVLink, PCIe, and InfiniBand serve different roles.

### Week 3: Network Fabrics

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Network Fabrics](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/network_fabrics/network_fabrics.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 03](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_03_communication/): Communication Topologies |
| **Due** | Lab 03 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Compare fat-tree, torus, and dragonfly topologies. Calculate the communication overhead of a given all-reduce pattern. Explain how network fabric design constrains parallelism strategies.

### Week 4: Distributed Storage

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Data Storage](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/data_storage/data_storage.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 04](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_04_data_storage/): The Storage Hierarchy |
| **Due** | Lab 04 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Design a distributed storage system that feeds thousands of accelerators without starvation. Calculate throughput requirements for a given training workload. Explain the tradeoffs between local SSD, networked storage, and object stores.

## Part II: Distributed Algorithms (Weeks 5–8) {#part-ii}

*Goal: Coordinate computation across thousands of nodes.*

### Week 5: Collective Communication

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Collective Communication](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/collective_communication/collective_communication.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 05](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_05_collective_communication/): Collective Communication |
| **Due** | Lab 05 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Trace ring all-reduce and state the conditions for its bandwidth efficiency. Calculate the time for an all-reduce operation given message size and network bandwidth. Explain how gradient compression reduces communication cost.

### Week 6: Distributed Training

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Distributed Training](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/distributed_training/distributed_training.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 06](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_06_dist_train/): The Parallelism Puzzle (3D Parallelism) |
| **Due** | Lab 06 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Trace an update through data, tensor, and pipeline parallel schedules. Calculate the communication-to-computation ratio for each parallelism strategy. Defend a feasible parallelism strategy for a given model size and cluster configuration, including its update semantics and time-to-quality assumptions.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Instructor Tip
Lab 06 is the centerpiece of the semester. Students discover that no single parallelism strategy wins — the optimal choice depends on model size, cluster topology, and communication bandwidth. Have them argue for their strategy in a class debate.
:::

### Week 7: Fault Tolerance

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Fault Tolerance](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/fault_tolerance/fault_tolerance.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 07](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_07_fault_tolerance/): When Failure Is Routine |
| **Due** | Lab 07 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Calculate the expected time-to-failure for a 10,000-GPU cluster. Design a checkpointing strategy that balances overhead and recovery time. Explain why fault tolerance is an engineering requirement, not an optional feature, at scale.

::: {.callout-note}
## Key Insight
At 10,000 nodes with a constant 0.1% daily failure probability per node, the expected count is ~10 failed nodes per day; the realized count varies. System design must budget for detection, valid recovery, and lost work alongside measures that reduce failure rates.
:::

### Week 8: Fleet Orchestration

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Fleet Orchestration](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/fleet_orchestration/fleet_orchestration.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 08](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_08_fleet_orch/): The Scheduling Trap |
| **Due** | Lab 08 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Explain how Slurm and Kubernetes manage heterogeneous cluster resources. Design a scheduling policy that maximizes cluster utilization while meeting SLA deadlines. Calculate the cost of fragmentation in a multi-tenant cluster.

## Part III: Deployment at Scale (Weeks 9–12) {#part-iii}

*Goal: Serve the world reliably.*

### Week 9: Performance Engineering

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Performance Engineering](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/performance_engineering/performance_engineering.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 09](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_09_perf_engineering/): Optimize the Path |
| **Due** | Lab 09 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Diagnose compute, memory, and execution overhead on a serving path using matched evidence. Compare fusion, tiling, precision, compilation, and batching under common memory and quality constraints. Defend a replica configuration and name the observation that could reverse the choice. Lab results are analytical estimates with supplied quality evidence; distributed-training calibration is covered in weeks 5–6.

### Week 10: Inference at Scale

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Inference at Scale](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/inference/inference.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 10](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_10_inference/): The Inference Economy |
| **Due** | Lab 10 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Account for model weights, KV-cache, and execution workspace under a stated concurrency and sequence-length workload. Identify when the KV-cache limits admission. Compare PagedAttention and continuous batching under memory, latency, and quality constraints.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Instructor Tip
Have students calculate: "How much GPU memory does serving GPT-3 (175B parameters) to 100 concurrent users at sequence length 2048 require?" The answer is large, and it motivates every optimization in this chapter.
:::

### Week 11: Edge Intelligence

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Edge Intelligence](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/edge_intelligence/edge_intelligence.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 11](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_11_edge_intelligence/): Edge Adaptation and Participation |
| **Due** | Lab 11 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Compare local and fleet adaptation under memory, energy, thermal, communication, and foreground-service budgets. Design a cohort-aware admission and participation policy. Distinguish completed-client coverage from validated learning quality and state which populations the updates represent.

### Week 12: Operations at Scale

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Ops at Scale](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/ops_scale/ops_scale.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 12](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_12_ops_scale/): The Silent Fleet |
| **Due** | Lab 12 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Design a monitoring and alerting system for a production ML fleet. Calculate the 3-year Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for a cluster configuration. Explain blue-green deployments and canary rollouts for ML models.

## Part IV: The Responsible Fleet (Weeks 13–16) {#part-iv}

*Goal: Manage the societal and environmental impact of scale.*

### Week 13: Security and Privacy

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Security & Privacy](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/security_privacy/security_privacy.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 13](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_13_security_privacy/): The Price of Privacy |
| **Due** | Lab 13 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Explain model inversion, membership inference, and adversarial attacks as systems problems. Calculate the throughput overhead of differential privacy. Design a secure serving pipeline with appropriate threat modeling.

### Week 14: Robust AI

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Robust AI](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/robust_ai/robust_ai.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 14](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_14_robust_ai/): The Robustness Budget |
| **Due** | Lab 14 Decision Log |

**Learning Objectives**: Define robustness as a systems property, not just a model property. Quantify the cost of adversarial defenses in throughput and latency. Interpret drift alerts alongside delayed labeled outcomes and replay evidence. Distinguish a feature-distribution change from demonstrated quality loss, and justify investigation or containment within the available evidence.

### Week 15: Sustainable and Responsible AI

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Sustainable AI](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/sustainable_ai/sustainable_ai.html) and [Responsible AI](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/responsible_ai/responsible_ai.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 15](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_15_sustainable_ai/) and [Lab 16](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_16_responsible_ai/): The Fairness Budget |
| **Due** | Lab 15 and Lab 16 Decision Logs + Capstone draft |

**Learning Objectives**: Calculate operational training emissions within a stated PUE and grid-carbon boundary. Compare feasible location or lifecycle alternatives over a common useful-work horizon. Interpret subgroup outcomes separately from audit coverage and review capacity. Defend a release, restriction, or deferral with a named owner, remedy, remaining uncertainty, and reevaluation trigger.

### Week 16: Capstone — Fleet Synthesis

| Component | Assignment |
|:---|:---|
| **Read** | [Conclusion](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/conclusion/conclusion.html) |
| **Lab** | [Lab 17](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/vol2/lab_17_fleet_synthesis/): The Fleet Synthesis (Capstone) |
| **Capstone** | Fleet Synthesis evidence packet and design report |
| **Due** | Final submission + design report |

**Capstone Specification**: Defend a bounded fleet repair using Lab 17's inherited evidence, scale and service stresses, equal-budget alternatives, and held-out replay. Submit the saved evidence packet and a design report explaining the chosen repair, a rejected alternative, remaining uncertainty, and a measurable reevaluation condition. A justified restricted rollout, deferral, or no-feasible conclusion is a valid result. Link the report to the assessed Lab 16 release record and fleet-governance challenge for affected-population requirements, authority, and remedy; Lab 17's physical and service checks do not establish those claims. The report may reuse earlier assessed cost, carbon, and time-to-quality analyses with their original boundaries. A complete frontier-system architecture project is an optional extension with separately specified evidence and workload.

| Component | Weight | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Lab Decision Logs** (Labs 01–16) | 40% | Sixteen evidence-based analyses; Lab 17 is assessed with the capstone |
| **Design Challenges** (4 major) | 30% | One per Part: cluster design, parallelism selection, serving architecture, fleet governance |
| **Capstone** | 30% | Fleet Synthesis evidence packet, design report, and presentation |
